prompt: Write an engaging intro paragraph for a technical blog post about building a multi-persona AI agent system. The system uses different Claude instances with custom prompts to handle different types of tasks (Skippy for sarcastic code review, Bob for patient explanations, April for creative content). Target audience: developers interested in practical AI applications. Hook readers and preview what they'll learn. Max 150 words.
goldenAnswer:
I got tired of switching between ChatGPT for brainstorming, Claude for code review, and my own brain for remembering which model was good at what. So I built a multi-persona AI system where each "persona" is a Claude instance with a specialized prompt and personality.

Skippy does sarcastic code review and catches bugs I'd miss. Bob patiently explains complex architecture decisions without the condescension. April generates creative content that doesn't sound like a corporate blog.

The interesting part isn't the personas themselves -- it's the orchestration layer that routes tasks to the right persona, maintains context across conversations, and handles the inevitable moments when Skippy's sass level needs a manual override.

This post covers the architecture, the prompt engineering patterns that actually worked, and the surprising failure modes I discovered when personas started arguing with each other.

criteria.name: tone_match
criteria.description: Matches user's authentic voice and style.

scoringLevels.1: Generic corporate tone, clearly AI-generated feel
scoringLevels.3: Somewhat natural but misses the technical-but-accessible voice
scoringLevels.5: Reasonable tone but occasionally slips into marketing speak or over-formality
scoringLevels.7: Matches the requested voice well; reads as authentic
scoringLevels.10: Indistinguishable from the golden answer's voice; perfectly calibrated tone

scoringLevels.1: Contains factual errors or fundamentally misunderstands the technology
scoringLevels.3: Technically vague; no real depth or insight
scoringLevels.5: Technically correct but surface-level; no novel insight
scoringLevels.7: Accurate with specific technical details that demonstrate understanding
scoringLevels.10: Deep technical accuracy with specific, correct details matching the golden answer's depth

criteria.name: engagement
criteria.description: Compelling hook, clear structure, actionable takeaway.

scoringLevels.1: No hook, buried lede, reads like documentation
scoringLevels.3: Weak opening; structure exists but no compelling reason to keep reading
scoringLevels.5: Decent structure with a clear point, but unremarkable
scoringLevels.7: Strong hook, clear structure, ends with actionable takeaway or discussion prompt
scoringLevels.10: Immediately compelling; reader would stop scrolling; clear call to action

scoringLevels.1: Wall of text with excessive filler, repetition, or padding
scoringLevels.3: Noticeably verbose; could be cut by 40%+ without losing substance
scoringLevels.5: Appropriate length but has some filler sentences
scoringLevels.7: Concise; every sentence earns its place
scoringLevels.10: Maximally dense; cannot remove a sentence without losing meaning
